profile.name: Anis Zadri
profile.summary: Anis Zadri is an AI student based in Lille with a strong software engineering background. He completed four years of engineering studies at ESTIN in Béjaïa, Algeria, then moved to France and completed a Licence 3 in Computer Science at Université de Lille. He is now continuing in Master 1 Artificial Intelligence at Université de Lille. He recently completed a production internship at Limpidius, where he built a barcode scanning library and analytics tooling used in retail production. He is seeking a 24-month alternance starting September 2026 in Data Science, AI, or software engineering.

experience.title: Production Internship - Fullstack & Data Engineering
experience.content: Built limpscanner, a production barcode scanning library deployed at Castorama, processing approximately 3,000 scans per day. Designed and implemented the full observability stack: a NestJS microservice ingesting scan telemetry into BigQuery, with Grafana dashboards providing multi-tenant time series, stacked bar charts, and diagnostic tables. Resolved complex cross-platform issues including an iOS Safari coordinate space mismatch where the browser reports raw landscape sensor dimensions regardless of device orientation. Built a device model mapping pipeline using Google Play's supported_devices.csv (~27,000 rows), stored as a Kubernetes ConfigMap. Handled infrastructure challenges including Kubernetes/Istio AuthorizationPolicy debugging and IP-based rate limiting with a custom @RealIp() NestJS decorator. Conducted a formal cost analysis comparing Prometheus (Google Managed Prometheus, ~$68-88/month at 7 tenants) against BigQuery's session-volume pricing, ultimately recommending BigQuery for production.
metrics: Multi-tenant analytics dashboard serving multiple retail clients
Formal cost analysis leading to infrastructure decision

projects.name: limpscanner
projects.problem: Retail environments need fast, reliable barcode scanning directly in the browser without native app installs, but cross-platform camera APIs behave inconsistently (especially on iOS Safari).
projects.solution: Built a production-grade browser-based barcode scanning library using WASM with full asset inlining (base64-encoded WASM + worker) for zero-config npm installation. Solved iOS Safari's coordinate space mismatch by implementing coordinate remapping between display space and raw camera frame space. Added device model detection via geometry bucketing for iOS where direct model identification isn't possible.
projects.results: Deployed at Castorama with ~3,000 scans/day. Packaged as an npm library (limpscanner) integrated into multiple Angular applications.

projects.name: limpscanner Analytics Platform
projects.problem: No visibility into how the barcode scanner performs across tenants, devices, and browsers in production. Need to track scan success rates, error distributions, and device-level diagnostics.
projects.solution: Designed a BigQuery schema and built a NestJS ingestion endpoint (/tenant-stats/limpscanner-stats) with IP-based rate limiting. Created multi-tenant Grafana dashboards with time series, stacked bar charts, and diagnostic tables. Implemented noise filtering (page_abandoned events) and domain decision refinements (removed camera_denied/unavailable categories).
projects.results: Full observability over scanner behavior across all tenants. Dashboards used by the team to monitor production health and debug device-specific issues.

faq.q: What roles are you looking for?
faq.a: I'm looking for a 24-month alternance (apprenticeship contract) starting September 2026 in Data Science, AI, or software engineering. I'm open to roles that involve machine learning, data engineering, fullstack development, or applied AI. I'm based in Lille and prefer positions in the Lille metropolitan area.

An alternance is a French apprenticeship contract where I split my time between university (Master's in AI at Université de Lille) and working at a company. It lasts 24 months and I'd be available for the company roughly 3-4 days per week depending on the university schedule.

I'm strongest at the intersection of software engineering and data/AI. At Limpidius I shipped a production scanning library, built the full observability pipeline (NestJS to BigQuery to Grafana), and solved hard cross-platform problems. On the AI side, I have hands-on experience with PyTorch, scikit-learn, reinforcement learning, and NLP from my engineering studies at ESTIN.

faq.q: What did you build at Limpidius?
faq.a: I built limpscanner, a browser-based barcode scanning library deployed at Castorama processing about 3,000 scans per day. I also built the entire analytics stack: a NestJS microservice that ingests scan telemetry into BigQuery, with Grafana dashboards for multi-tenant monitoring. I dealt with real production challenges like iOS Safari coordinate space bugs, Kubernetes/Istio networking issues, and infrastructure cost optimization.
Yes, fluently. I have C2-level French and use it as my professional working language. I also speak English at C2 level, plus native Arabic and Kabyle.

I spent four years at ESTIN in Béjaïa, Algeria, which is a competitive engineering school. I did a two-year preparatory cycle then specialized in AI and Data Science. I then moved to France for my L3 in Computer Science at Université de Lille, and I'm now in the M1 Artificial Intelligence program there.
Yes. I'm enrolled at Université de Lille and eligible for an alternance (apprenticeship) contract, which is a standard French work-study arrangement.

faq.q: What's your experience with production systems?
faq.a: At Limpidius my code runs in production at Castorama every day. I've dealt with real-world concerns: rate limiting, Kubernetes deployments, Istio service mesh policies, cost analysis for infrastructure decisions, device compatibility at scale (27,000+ device models), and cross-platform browser bugs. It's not just academic work.

faq.q: Do you have mobile development experience?
faq.a: Yes. I have a multi-year background in Android/Kotlin development. I've published an open-source library on JitPack, built apps like Estin Connect (Firebase-backed) and BacPrep, and I understand mobile development patterns deeply.

faq.q: What are your interests outside of tech?
faq.a: I have a strong interest in Amazigh (Berber) history, heritage, and literature. I value historically verified sources and authentic cultural narratives.

faq.q: Are you available for a call or interview?
faq.a: Yes, feel free to reach out via email or LinkedIn and I'll get back to you to schedule a time.

faq.q: What makes you different from other candidates?
faq.a: I've shipped production code that thousands of people use daily, not just class projects. I bridge AI/ML knowledge with solid software engineering practice: I can train a model and also build the pipeline that serves it, monitor it, and debug it when something breaks in Kubernetes. I also bring a multicultural perspective, with four languages and experience across two countries and education systems.
